title: DISTRIBUTIONALLY ROBUST NEURAL NETWORKS FOR GROUP SHIFTS: ON THE IMPORTANCE OF REGULARIZATION FOR WORST-CASE GENERALIZATION

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating worst-group test accuracy on the CelebA dataset by predicting hair color while treating gender (male/female) as a spuriously correlated demographic attribute to measure performance disparities.

Evaluating worst-group test accuracy on a custom Waterbirds image dataset by predicting bird categories (waterbird vs. landbird) while treating image background (water vs. land) as a spuriously correlated dataset artifact.

Evaluating worst-group test accuracy on the MultiNLI dataset by measuring the model's reliance on spurious correlations between inference labels (e.g., contradiction) and specific syntactic artifacts (e.g., presence of negation words).
